newsitem.title: FRANCE: France will not authorise gene-crop production.
newsitem.headline: France will not authorise gene-crop production.

text.p: French farm minister Philippe Vasseur said on Wednesday that France, which recently cleared the marketing of genetically-modified maize, will not authorise the cultivation of gene-altered crops this year.

"At this stage we must proceed with caution....we will not authorise the cultivation of gene-modified varieties this year," Vasseur told a news conference on the highlights of the new framework law on agriculture.
Vasseur however specified that cultivation of gene-altered crops will go on in France on an experimental basis. "There must be experiental cultivation for research but not for marketing."
"At this stage we must be totally responsible. We do not know what can be the effects of the cultivation of gene-modified maize," he said.
France cleared the marketing of gene-modified maize last week developed by Swiss firm Ciba-Ceigy and adapted to resist the corn borer pest.
The clearance came after France made the labelling of gene-altered organisms and derived products mandatory.
The authorisation applied only to the import of maize and derived products and not to its cultivation.
In December the European Union cleared imports of genetically-modified maize for sale in Europe.
The EU is to issue guidelines on the labelling of goods containing gene-modified products by mid-March.
Pressed by consumer and environmental groups concerns over the possible risks to health and environment, France did not wait for the EU labelling rules and issued its own code.
